Shape.Text: Proper care of patient positioning should be followed in order to keep the scan field of view in the most optimized section of the body coil (refer to image below)

Shape.Name: Procedure
Shape.Text:
The design of the body coil can be compared to a high pass filter. The inductors form the bars in the birdcage and the capacitors form the end rings.
The wall of the body coil is only about 1/4 inch thick. Consequently when the patient is touching the bore, his body is very close to the coil conductors. Since the patient's body is mostly water and water has a very high dielectric constant, the capacitance of the coil in close proximity to the patient is increased significantly. This shifts the resonance of some of the coil modes and causes large differences between the currents. When the currents are unbalanced, B1 homogeneity suffers and shading occurs. Other effects include increased RF transmit power and reduced SNR.
These effects can be essentially eliminated by placing pads between the patient and the coil. It is very important to understand that detuning can occur even though the point where the patient is close to the coil is far away from the scan plane.
NOTE: Pads should provide at least 1/2 inch of spacing with the pads compressed. Pads that are only 1/2 inch thick before compression are not adequate. Use of a thick pad between the patient and the cradle can cause problems with larger patients because the pad raises the patient closer to the upper inside portion of the body coil. On some patients the cradle pad should be removed. Also, there are two cables connecting between the body hybrid and the body coil. These cables create magnetic fields perpendicular to one another. If one of the cables or the hybrid has gone bad, then shading will occur. These failure modes include the TG increasing by 3dB (30 counts) and the SPT Body SNR results decreasing by about 40%.

Shape.Name: Bordered rectangle
Shape.Text: First applications concern is if patient has ferrous material on or in them. Shading caused by the following items would be dependent and random. The ferrous material at such a close proximity to the area of interest changes the magnetic field causing shading. An example of shading due to metal is on the bottom of this page. Here is a partial list of ferrous materials known to cause shading: * Patient implanted metal * Underwire Bras * Mascara * Body Piercings * Make-up * Hearing Aids * Oral Bridgework, excessive cavities * Some form of tattoos * "Slimfast" diet drink or a vitamin B injection * "Spandex" clothing

Shape.Name: Procedure.6
Shape.Text: Due to the structure of the head, head imaging has some unique application concerns. Magnetic susceptibilities of the sinus and IAC (Inner Auditory Ear Canal) tend to cause intensity loss in signal especially in Gradient Echoes, Low Variable Bandwidth and EPI scans. Gradient Echoes do not use refocusing 180 degree pulses . The 180 degree pulses cause the proton spins to regroup which minimizes most types of magnetic susceptibilities (T2 * ) .

Shape.Name: Create request
Shape.Text: These effects will be exaggerated in higher field strengths. If shading occurs around any tissue/air interface such as the sinus or IAC , the problem is applications related . Use a spin echo or higher bandwidth.

Shape.Text: Bench testing the cable is normally a reliable way of determining if it is functional, but even if it passes here it may still be defective (breaking down under high RF power). Trying a replacement part should be considered

Shape.Name: Sheet.3
Shape.Text: Diagonal or shading on a 45 degree angle indicates that the body coil is transmitting in linear mode. This section will try a quick inspection of items that commonly have failed causing this problem

Shape.Name: Create request
Shape.Text:
Inspect the RF connectors at the Hybrid (J1, J3, J4) for signs of arcing. Any graying, blackening, or other questionable appearance should dictate the replacement of the cable or associated mating part. Any RF connector should be visually brand new in appearance (shiny chrome, no tarnishing, etc.). Inspect the 90 degree elbow and the cable connector carefully. You should not be able to twist the connector with thumb or finger pressure.
Also, there are two cables connecting between the body hybrid and the body coil. These cables create magnetic fields perpendicular to one another. If one of the cables or the hybrid has gone bad, then shading will occur. These failure modes include the TG increasing by 3 dB (30 counts) and the SPT Body SNR results decreasing by about 40%.

Shape.Name: Create request.4
Shape.Text: Disassemble the head coil and inspect the Isolation boards, the chip capacitors and the Head coil's hybrid. Look for any loose connections, cracked solder joints (especially near the rigid coax connection since over tightening will crack the board), and/or burnt charring of components and connections.

Shape.Name: Procedure
Shape.Text: Visual inspection is normally a reliable way of determining if a problem exists. However the part still may be defective if a defect is not discovered (it may break down under high power conditions). Trying a replacement part should be considered
